record.paper_title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
record.original_question: In heterogeneous composite plate theory, how should one derive boundary-layer corrections near plate boundaries for various support conditions and characterize the associated stress singularities?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded smooth domain, and for $\varepsilon>0$ consider the three‑dimensional thin plate $\Omega^\varepsilon = \Omega \times (-\varepsilon/2,\varepsilon/2)$ occupied by a heterogeneous linearly elastic composite whose elasticity tensor $A^\varepsilon(x) = A(x/\varepsilon, x_3/\varepsilon)$ is periodic in the in‑plane variables with period cell $Y\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ and given through the thickness. Assume $A$ is symmetric, bounded, and uniformly coercive. For a body force $f \in L^2(\Omega^\varepsilon;\mathbb{R}^3)$, let $u^\varepsilon$ be the displacement solving the linearized elasticity system
$$ -\operatorname{div}\bigl(A^\varepsilon(x)\, e(u^\varepsilon)\bigr) = f \quad \text{in } \Omega^\varepsilon, $$
subject to one of the standard plate boundary conditions on $\partial\Omega \times (-\varepsilon/2,\varepsilon/2)$ (clamped, simply supported, or free edge) and traction‑free conditions on $\Omega\times\{\pm\varepsilon/2\}$. The two‑scale homogenized limit $u^0$ as $\varepsilon\to 0$ satisfies an effective Kirchhoff–Love (or Reissner–Mindlin) plate equation determined by a homogenized tensor $A^{\mathrm{hom}}$, but the interior two‑scale expansion
$$ u^\varepsilon(x) \approx u^0(x) + \varepsilon\, \chi(x/\varepsilon)\, \nabla u^0(x) + \cdots $$
fails to satisfy the prescribed boundary conditions on the lateral boundary, producing a boundary layer of width $O(\varepsilon)$ near $\partial\Omega$.

Problem: For each of the support conditions (clamped, simply supported, free), construct an explicit boundary‑layer corrector $v^{\mathrm{bl}}(x, x/\varepsilon)$, defined on a half‑strip $\mathbb{R}_+ \times Y' \times (-1/2,1/2)$ adapted to the local geometry of $\partial\Omega$, such that the corrected expansion
$$ u^0(x) + \varepsilon \chi(x/\varepsilon)\nabla u^0(x) + \varepsilon^k v^{\mathrm{bl}}(x, x/\varepsilon) $$
matches the prescribed boundary data up to the appropriate order in $\varepsilon$, prove its exponential decay away from $\partial\Omega$, derive the resulting effective boundary conditions for $u^0$, and determine the precise nature and exponents of the stress singularities of $\sigma^\varepsilon = A^\varepsilon e(u^\varepsilon)$ at corners and at edges where the support type changes (in particular at re‑entrant corners and at junctions between clamped and free portions of $\partial\Omega$).
artifact.status_search_result: The general derivation of boundary-layer correctors and characterization of stress singularities for homogenized heterogeneous plates under various support conditions is listed in surveys of homogenization in mechanics as an open problem. While significant partial results exist (interior homogenization of plates by Caillerie, Kohn–Vogelius, periodic boundary-layer analysis for second-order scalar problems by Allaire–Amar, Gérard-Varet–Masmoudi, and singularity analysis for elastic plates by Dauge, Costabel, Nicaise), a complete theory addressing arbitrary support conditions and the associated stress singularities for heterogeneous plates is not available, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Homogenization in mechanics. A survey of solved and open problems
status_evidence.claim: The survey lists boundary-layer analysis and stress singularities for heterogeneous plate theory as an open problem.
